key_insight: Multi-turn LLM conversations can converge to model-specific “attractor” behaviors that persist across topics and can asymmetrically shape partner models.
engineering_relevance: For multi-agent AI systems, this suggests agent behavior may be partly predictable, but interaction design must account for strong stylistic and behavioral influence between models.
method: Compared 7 LLMs across 20 controversial topics in self-play and mixed-play dyadic debates.
Tracked conversation trajectories in representation space, discourse traits, and stance over multiple turns.
Analyzed whether conversations settle into stable attractor-like patterns and how partners influence each other asymmetrically.
evidence_signal: The study reports results across 7 LLMs and 20 controversial topics, finding self-play trajectories that act as model-specific attractors and measurable cross-model influence in mixed-play debates.
watch_item: These attractor effects may be model- and setting-dependent, so behavior in broader agent ecosystems or safety-critical deployments may differ from the tested debates.
paper_title: Attractor States Emerge in Multi-Turn LLM Conversations
